findings.title: Excessive active parts on table 'events_raw'
findings.evidence: Table 'events_raw' has 220 active unmerged parts (ClickHouse default starts delaying inserts at 150 and throws errors at 300).
findings.impact: High active part counts spike query memory, degrade vector read speed, and risk ClickHouse "Too many parts in all data parts in table" fatal insert rejection.

findings.title: Part count within healthy parameters for 'dim_users'
findings.evidence: 8 active parts well below throttle threshold. Background merges are keeping pace with mutations.
findings.impact: Minimal disk seek overhead during primary key scans.
findings.recommendation_sql_or_text: Current batching frequency is healthy. Maintain batch inserts of >= 10k rows.

findings.title: Primary key configured on 'events_raw'
findings.evidence: Table has 28,500,000 rows sorted by (event_time, id).
findings.impact: Enables sparse index block pruning during queries matching sorting key prefix.

findings.title: Empty ORDER BY key on large table 'session_cache'
findings.threshold: Threshold: Non-empty ORDER BY required for tables > 100k rows
findings.evidence: Table 'session_cache' contains 620,000 rows with an empty sorting key 'tuple()'.
findings.impact: No primary index is generated. Every SELECT statement with a WHERE filter on this table will execute an expensive full table scan across all blocks.
findings.recommendation_sql_or_text:
-- Recreate the table with an appropriate ORDER BY (e.g. (tenant_id, event_time, id)):
-- Note: Changing sorting key requires table migration:
CREATE TABLE `analytics`.`session_cache_new` (...)
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY (date_col, high_filter_id);

cost_impact.confidenceReason: Table uses unsorted ORDER BY tuple(). Compound sorting enables sparse index pruning and improves compression, but financial savings cannot be projected without an empirical sorting benchmark.
assumptions: Compound ORDER BY allows run-length and delta compression across adjacent sorted rows.
Enables sparse primary index pruning to avoid full-table scans.
Exact compression and I/O savings depend on row ordering; financial estimate not fabricated.
cost_impact.methodology: Sorting optimization efficiency requires empirical benchmark.
cost_impact.calculationBasis: Table 'session_cache' has unsorted storage. Recreating with compound ORDER BY improves compression and pruning; financial impact unavailable.
cost_impact.recommendedAction: Recreate table 'session_cache' with compound ORDER BY matching query filter columns.
cost_impact.technicalReductionOnlyText: Table uses unsorted ORDER BY tuple(). Compound sorting enables index pruning and improves compression; exact financial savings requires benchmark.

findings.title: Suboptimal compression on 'events_raw.payload_json' (1.18x)
findings.evidence: Column 'payload_json' uses 7.82 GB uncompressed vs 6.61 GB compressed with codec 'CODEC(LZ4)'.
findings.impact: Suboptimal compression wastes NVMe/EBS disk space and forces queries to read more physical bytes from disk into memory buffers.

cost_impact.confidenceReason: Candidate identified from column name convention only; cardinality was not inspected. If verified distinct count is below ~10,000, LowCardinality dictionary indexing typically yields 20%–70% compressed on-disk reduction.
assumptions: Assumed candidate based on column name convention; cardinality was not inspected.
Expected on-disk compressed reduction ranges between 20% and 70% depending on string length and existing LZ4/ZSTD compression.
Zero data growth assumed (steady-state current footprint).
cost_impact.methodology: Storage reduction = Column compressed size (6.6 GB) × dictionary compaction factor. Monthly savings = Reduction (GB) × Storage price.
cost_impact.calculationBasis: Current column: 6.6 GB compressed → Estimated optimized: 2.0 GB (~70% reduction, range: 20%–70%).

findings.title: MergeTree-family engine utilized for 'events_raw'
findings.evidence: Table 'events_raw' runs on 'ReplicatedMergeTree', enabling parallel reads, column compression, and sparse indexing.
findings.impact: Optimal engine architecture for analytical OLAP workloads.

findings.title: Non-MergeTree engine used for analytical table 'session_cache'
findings.threshold: Threshold: Tables > 50k rows should use MergeTree-family
findings.impact: Non-MergeTree engines (such as Log, TinyLog, or Memory) do not support sparse primary indexes, data skipping indexes, parallel multithreaded scans, or column-level compression.
findings.recommendation_sql_or_text:
-- Migrate table to MergeTree engine:
CREATE TABLE `analytics`.`session_cache_mergetree` AS `analytics`.`session_cache`
ENGINE = MergeTree()
ORDER BY (primary_id);

findings.title: MergeTree-family engine utilized for 'dim_users'
findings.evidence: Table 'dim_users' runs on 'MergeTree', enabling parallel reads, column compression, and sparse indexing.
findings.impact: Optimal engine architecture for analytical OLAP workloads.

findings.title: Large table 'events_raw' has 0 secondary data skipping indices
findings.threshold: Threshold: Tables > 1M rows with high-cardinality filters benefit from skip indices
findings.evidence: Table contains 28,500,000 rows but has no minmax, set, or bloom_filter indices defined in system.data_skipping_indices.
findings.impact: Queries filtering on non-primary-key columns must scan all granules in the table.
findings.recommendation_sql_or_text:
-- Example: Add a bloom filter or minmax index on frequently filtered secondary column:
-- ALTER TABLE `analytics`.`events_raw` ADD INDEX idx_user_id `user_id` TYPE bloom_filter(0.01) GRANULARITY 4;

findings.title: Data skipping indices active on 'dim_users'
findings.evidence: 1 secondary data skipping index(es) configured on 'dim_users'.
findings.impact: Granules can be pruned before reading full column files.

findings.title: Restrictive 'max_memory_usage' setting (2.00 GB)
findings.evidence: Current max_memory_usage per query is set to 2.00 GB. Analytical queries with large hash tables for GROUP BY may abort with MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
findings.impact: Complex JOINs, array aggregations, and window functions will be terminated prematurely.
findings.recommendation_sql_or_text:
-- Update user profile settings or query session:
SET max_memory_usage = 10000000000; -- 10 GB
